### Recommendation
- Argentina's defensive efforts were evident in their ability to force opponents to take more difficult shots from outside the penalty box
- Argentina's offensive prowess is reflected in the higher number of goals conceded by their opponents
- Argentina's effective goal-scoring ability put pressure on their opponents, challenging to gain less possession of the ball

### Evidence

#### The Data
- With a total of 64 matches, 30 matches were looked at being the games Argentina played and also the opponents of Argentina and the games in which they played
- Six variables were taken into consideration including:
  - Possession of opponent team
  - Goals conceded of opponent team team
  - Goals scored of opponent team
  - Total Shots on target of opponent team 
  - Total shots inside the penalty box of opponent team
  - Total shots outside the penalty box of opponent team
- Teams that didn't play against Argentina weren't included (e.g. Portugal)


<br>

```{r, echo = FALSE}
ggplot(data, aes(x = Teams)) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = Total_Shots, fill = "Shots Inside Penalty Box"),
           stat = "identity", width = 0.5) +
  geom_bar(aes(y = Shots_Out, fill = "Shots Outside Penalty Box"),
           stat = "identity", width = 0.5) +
  ylim(0, 20) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Shot Statistics",
    x = "Games",
    y = "Average Shots per game",
    fill = "Shot Location"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Shots Inside Penalty Box" = "#49BCE3",
               "Shots Outside Penalty Box" = "#FEC310")
  ) +
  theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.title = element_text(color = "black", size = 12, face = "bold"), axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# For the table below, I had made a mock table in word and counted the values individually and triple checking it to ensure it was accurate
```

### Analysis
- The graph took into account the total number of shots and provided a more detailed examination by highlighting shots taken both inside and outside the penalty box
- Argentina's opponents often recorded a lower average number of shots per game when facing Argentina, demonstrating Argentina's proficiency in preventing their opponents from taking shots
- The teams that encountered Argentina during the group stage (Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Poland) encountered difficulties in generating a considerable number of shots
  - This can be observed through a comparison with matches where teams did not face Argentina, as they typically recorded more than double the number of shots compared to when playing against Argentina
  - These teams also exhibited a higher proportion of shots taken from outside the penalty box, which underscores Argentina's exceptional defense in restricting easier shots and compelling opponents to attempt more challenging shots
- Top teams like France, Croatia, and Netherlands encountered difficulties in generating shots against Argentina, further reinforcing Argentina's exceptional defense against high-caliber offensive players

### Analysis
- To refine the data set for analysis, data filtering was performed to include only the matches involving Argentina's opponents and their respective encounters with Argentina  
    - This approach allows us to focus specifically on the games played by Argentina's opponents and the corresponding matches between Argentina and each opponent
- Teams that faced Argentina consistently exhibited a significantly lower possession rate compared to matches where they did not face them 
   - This observation underscores Argentina's effectiveness in maintaining control of the ball throughout the game, limiting the opportunities for their opponents to assert their own possession
- Moreover, even when teams like Croatia managed to average higher possession against Argentina, they still encountered difficulties in creating more scoring opportunities
   - Additionally, they conceded a significant number of goals, highlighting Argentina's ability to capitalize on their opponents' vulnerabilities and convert their chances into goals

### Appendix: Defense of Approach
#####  Client


- Soccer analysts use data to gain insights, enhance understanding, and make informed decisions about various aspects of the game hence this choice made sense for data about the 2022 FIFA World Cup
- To accommodate to the interests of soccer analysts, a data analysis focused on the performance of World Cup winners was considered, as it is a commonly examined topic in the sport of soccer

#### Statistical Analysis

- By comparing Argentina's performance against their opponents to the opponents' performance in other games, the analysis highlights Argentina's dominance and superiority throughout the tournament
- The stats of possession, goals scored, shot attempts, and goals conceded emphasize Argentina's superior performance and their ability to outperform their opponents in key areas of the game
- In the context of analyzing Argentina's performance, the choice to use the mean instead of the median or standard deviation was more valuable as it would better demonstrate Argentina's performance in those categories



##### Limitations 


- Doesn't include all teams in the World Cup as it was done to ensure the data would look at the affect Argentina had on opponents they had versed 
- The sample of games in which Argentina played against these opponents consists of only a single match
